title: Oklahoma Sooners All-Time Bowl Record: 31-26-1 in 58 Games
question: What is Oklahoma's all-time bowl record?
answer: Oklahoma's all-time bowl record is 31-26-1 in 58 bowl games, a mark unchanged since the 2024 Armed Forces Bowl because OU's 2025 playoff game in Norman is not counted as a bowl. Its 58 appearances ranked fourth nationally entering that 2024 bowl.
summary: Oklahoma is 31-26-1 in 58 bowl games, fourth nationally in appearances. Here are its New Year's Six totals, record bowl streak and playoff results.
body: Oklahoma's bowl history stretches from a 17-0 loss to Tennessee in the January 1939 Orange Bowl to the 2024 Armed Forces Bowl, the program's 58th bowl game. OU's official game notes listed the Sooners at 31-25-1 entering that game, with their 58 appearances ranking fourth nationally and their 31 wins tied for fourth. Navy won 21-20 after Oklahoma scored with six seconds left and failed on the two-point try, leaving the all-time mark at 31-26-1.

The lone tie came in the 1970 Astro-Bluebonnet Bowl, a 24-24 game with Alabama. The Orange Bowl has been OU's most frequent destination. Of the 58 bowls, 39 came in games that now make up the New Year's Six: 20 Orange Bowls, eight Sugar, five Fiesta, three Cotton, two Rose and one Peach. That count does not include the January 2009 BCS title game against Florida.

The Bob Stoops era built the longest bowl streak in school history. Beginning with Stoops' first season in 1999, Oklahoma went to 26 consecutive bowls through 2024, shattering the old school record of eight straight from the 1975-82 seasons under Barry Switzer.

The playoff era has been tougher. OU reached College Football Playoff semifinals after the 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2019 seasons and lost all four. In December 2025, the Sooners hosted Alabama in a first-round playoff game in Norman and lost 34-24. That campus game is listed separately from the 58 bowl games counted above.
